CRITICAL
Hardcoded fallback secret for JWT_SECRET
server.js:13
[proofscan.hardcoded-fallback-secret]
`process.env.JWT_SECRET || '<literal>'` supplies a hardcoded secret whenever JWT_SECRET is
unset in the environment, assigned to `JWT_SECRET`. The literal is committed to the
repository, so it is known to anyone who can read the source. Secret scanners tuned for
issued-credential formats and high entropy do not flag values like this, which is why it
is checked as a pattern rather than by value.
code:
process.env.JWT_SECRET || '<redacted: 25 chars>'
exploitability:
Requires the deployment to be missing JWT_SECRET. If it is, the
signing key is public: an attacker mints a token for any user id and authenticates as
them, with no credential needed. Verify which environments actually set JWT_SECRET before
downgrading this.
status: unverified-flagged · detected by: builtin · CWE-798, CWE-1188
HIGH
Hardcoded fallback secret for API_SECRET

[proofscan.hardcoded-fallback-secret]
`process.env.API_SECRET || '<literal>'` supplies a hardcoded secret whenever API_SECRET is
unset in the environment, assigned to `FAKE_AI_API_KEY`. The literal is committed to the
repository, so it is known to anyone who can read the source. Secret scanners tuned for
issued-credential formats and high entropy do not flag values like this, which is why it
is checked as a pattern rather than by value.
code:
process.env.API_SECRET || '<redacted: 16 chars>'
exploitability:

status: unverified-flagged · detected by: builtin · CWE-798, CWE-1188
HIGH
CORS reflects any origin while allowing credentials
server.js:18
[proofscan.cors-credentials-reflected-origin]
CORS is configured with `origin: true`, which echoes the request Origin header back,
together with `credentials: true`. Any website a logged-in user visits can then make
credentialed cross-origin requests to this API and read the responses, because the browser
is told that site is an allowed origin. Replace the reflected origin with an explicit
allowlist of the origins the application is actually served from.
code:
cors({ origin: true, credentials: true })
exploitability:
Requires a victim with a live session to visit a page the
attacker controls. No credential theft and no network position needed: the attacker's page
issues `fetch(target, {credentials: 'include'})` and reads the authenticated response.
Cookie-based sessions are directly affected; a session held only in localStorage is not
reachable this way, so confirm how sessions are carried before rating this in your own
environment.
status: unverified-flagged · detected by: builtin · CWE-942, CWE-346
HIGH
Authorisation-ordering defect in DELETE /api/tasks/:id
[VERIFIED EXPLOITABLE]
server.js:223
[proofscan.authorization-ordering]
Operation DELETE on notes at line 223 runs with a filter that is not constrained to the
authenticated caller, and its identifier comes from request input. No caller-scoped read
executes before it, so nothing has established that the caller owns the resource.
Determined by deterministic ordering analysis, not by a model.
Exploit outline: Authenticate as any user. Call DELETE /api/tasks/<id> with the identifier
of a resource belonging to a different user. The handler reaches the DELETE on notes
before any ownership check can stop it.
Expected impact: Rows in notes associated with the victim's resource are deleted. The
attacker's own response status may still indicate failure, so impact must be confirmed by
reading state back as the victim rather than by trusting the attacker's response code.
Assessed by the heuristic reasoner (confidence: medium). This is a candidate until an
automated exploit has run against a sandboxed copy and demonstrated the impact — see the
verification status on this finding.
code:
db.prepare('DELETE FROM notes WHERE task_id = ?').run(taskId)
exploitability:
Authenticate as any user. Call DELETE /api/tasks/<id> with the
identifier of a resource belonging to a different user. The handler reaches the DELETE on
notes before any ownership check can stop it.
verified:
Identity B issued DELETE /api/tasks/1 against identity A's resource
and received 404 (an apparent rejection). Reading A's state back as A, 1 child record(s)
were destroyed — a cross-user mutation. The attacker’s error status would hide this from
any check that trusted the response code. Demonstrated against a sandboxed copy of the
target; the verdict is the victim's own read-back, not the attacker's status.
status: verified-exploitable
· detected by: reasoner:heuristic · CWE-639, CWE-285, CWE-863
